minted_by.lane: ChatGPT Pro subscription, Sol state worker

cards.front: Complete the guidance about avoidance and skids, beginning with “The handbook identifies braking, steering and acceleration as”.
cards.back: The handbook identifies braking, steering and acceleration as options for avoiding a crash or reducing its impact.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about avoidance and skids, beginning with “ABS helps the vehicle stop without skidding while preserving”.
cards.back: ABS helps the vehicle stop without skidding while preserving steering control; follow the owner’s instructions for its use.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about avoidance and skids, beginning with “For the handbook’s ABS emergency-braking procedure, press”.
cards.back: For the handbook’s ABS emergency-braking procedure, press the brake pedal hard and keep pressure applied.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about avoidance and skids, beginning with “An ABS pedal may vibrate or produce clicking”.
cards.back: An ABS pedal may vibrate or produce clicking during operation, which the handbook describes as normal.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about avoidance and skids, beginning with “Steering remains possible while using ABS, and a”.
cards.back: Steering remains possible while using ABS, and a vehicle without ABS requires its own manual’s braking procedure.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about avoidance and skids, beginning with “To steer around a hazard, hold the wheel with”.
cards.back: To steer around a hazard, hold the wheel with both hands and aim toward the intended path while avoiding other traffic.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about avoidance and skids, beginning with “After clearing the hazard, countersteer to”.
cards.back: After clearing the hazard, countersteer to straighten and regain control before slowing.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about avoidance and skids, beginning with “Acceleration may be needed to avoid a vehicle”.
cards.back: Acceleration may be needed to avoid a vehicle about to strike from the rear or side.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about avoidance and skids, beginning with “A skid can result from excessive speed”.
cards.back: A skid can result from excessive speed for conditions, abrupt stopping or lost tire grip.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about avoidance and skids, beginning with “When a skid begins, release pressure on the”.
cards.back: When a skid begins, release pressure on the brake or accelerator and look toward the desired path.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about avoidance and skids, beginning with “If the wheels leave the pavement, avoid a panic”.
cards.back: If the wheels leave the pavement, avoid a panic return, slow gradually and steer back only when safe.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about mechanical emergencies, beginning with “Follow the vehicle owner’s maintenance”.
cards.back: Follow the vehicle owner’s maintenance schedule to reduce malfunction risk.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about mechanical emergencies, beginning with “The handbook warns against driving with a brake warning”.
cards.back: The handbook warns against driving with a brake warning illuminated and treats it as a reason to investigate brake operation.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about mechanical emergencies, beginning with “If brakes fail while moving, the handbook directs gradual”.
cards.back: If brakes fail while moving, the handbook directs gradual parking-brake application to avoid locking the rear wheels and readiness to release it if a skid starts.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about mechanical emergencies, beginning with “If the parking-brake response fails, the handbook next says”.
cards.back: If the parking-brake response fails, the handbook next says to turn off the engine and find a safe place off the road to stop.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about mechanical emergencies, beginning with “Do not continue driving a”.
cards.back: Do not continue driving a vehicle whose brakes do not work.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about mechanical emergencies, beginning with “A blowout is a rapid loss of tire air;”.
cards.back: A blowout is a rapid loss of tire air; a front blowout pulls sharply toward that side, while a rear blowout may wobble, shake and pull toward it.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about mechanical emergencies, beginning with “For a blowout, hold the wheel firmly, maintain a”.
cards.back: For a blowout, hold the wheel firmly, maintain a straight path, ease off the accelerator and let speed fall gradually.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about mechanical emergencies, beginning with “Avoid braking during a blowout, allowing the vehicle”.
cards.back: Avoid braking during a blowout, allowing the vehicle to slow naturally and braking gently only if necessary.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about mechanical emergencies, beginning with “After a blowout, leave the road at a safe”.
cards.back: After a blowout, leave the road at a safe location if possible, activate emergency flashers and replace the tire.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about mechanical emergencies, beginning with “If the engine stops while driving, keep a firm”.
cards.back: If the engine stops while driving, keep a firm grip because steering may become harder but remains possible.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about mechanical emergencies, beginning with “After engine failure, find an escape path, brake”.
cards.back: After engine failure, find an escape path, brake steadily instead of hard and pull off the road.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about mechanical emergencies, beginning with “Once stopped after engine failure, try restarting; if it”.
cards.back: Once stopped after engine failure, try restarting; if it fails, raise the hood, use emergency flashers and call for help.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about mechanical emergencies, beginning with “The handbook’s stuck-accelerator sequence starts with switching the”.
cards.back: The handbook’s stuck-accelerator sequence starts with switching the engine off, selecting Neutral and finding an escape path.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about mechanical emergencies, beginning with “Its stuck-accelerator procedure then calls for smooth steering, gentle”.
cards.back: Its stuck-accelerator procedure then calls for smooth steering, gentle braking and leaving the roadway, with service-center pedal repair before driving again.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about mechanical emergencies, beginning with “For a highway breakdown, make the vehicle visible”.
cards.back: For a highway breakdown, make the vehicle visible and notify authorities by phone or another available device.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about mechanical emergencies, beginning with “Move a broken-down vehicle away”.
cards.back: Move a broken-down vehicle away from traffic and activate emergency flashers.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about mechanical emergencies, beginning with “The handbook places breakdown-warning flares about two hundred”.
cards.back: The handbook places breakdown-warning flares about two hundred to three hundred feet behind the disabled vehicle.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about mechanical emergencies, beginning with “If headlights fail, try the switch several times; if”.
cards.back: If headlights fail, try the switch several times; if that fails, use available flashers, turn signals or fog lamps and leave the road promptly.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about crash-scene protection, beginning with “An uninvolved driver should not stop at a crash”.
cards.back: An uninvolved driver should not stop at a crash when emergency help is already present, but should keep watching for people near the road.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about crash-scene protection, beginning with “Do not travel to a crash, fire or disaster”.
cards.back: Do not travel to a crash, fire or disaster merely to look, because spectators may block rescue vehicles.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about crash-scene protection, beginning with “A driver involved in a crash must stop and”.
cards.back: A driver involved in a crash must stop and must try to find the owner after striking a parked vehicle.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about crash-scene protection, beginning with “Notify police when anyone is injured or killed; an”.
cards.back: Notify police when anyone is injured or killed; an involved driver must not leave before police obtain the needed crash information.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about crash-scene protection, beginning with “The handbook suggests carrying an emergency kit”.
cards.back: The handbook suggests carrying an emergency kit with warning flares, first-aid supplies and basic tools.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about crash-scene protection, beginning with “Stop at or near the crash site and move”.
cards.back: Stop at or near the crash site and move a drivable vehicle off the roadway to avoid blocking traffic or causing another crash.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about crash-scene protection, beginning with “Do not stand or walk in”.
cards.back: Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes at a crash scene.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about crash-scene protection, beginning with “Turn off wrecked-vehicle ignitions and do not”.
cards.back: Turn off wrecked-vehicle ignitions and do not smoke nearby because spilled fuel may ignite.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about crash-scene protection, beginning with “Stay away from fallen power”.
cards.back: Stay away from fallen power lines on or near the road.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about crash-scene protection, beginning with “Use flares or other warning devices”.
cards.back: Use flares or other warning devices to keep approaching traffic from becoming involved.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about crash-scene protection, beginning with “For injuries, call police and emergency medical or”.
cards.back: For injuries, call police and emergency medical or rescue help and report any fire when calling.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about collision mitigation, beginning with “Lap and shoulder belts are the handbook’s primary advice”.
cards.back: Lap and shoulder belts are the handbook’s primary advice for reducing injury when a collision cannot be avoided.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about collision mitigation, beginning with “For a rear impact, press against the seatback, place”.
cards.back: For a rear impact, press against the seatback, place the head against the restraint and prepare to brake against being pushed into another vehicle.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about collision mitigation, beginning with “For a side impact, the handbook says belts help”.
cards.back: For a side impact, the handbook says belts help retain position while the driver prepares to steer or brake against another collision.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about collision mitigation, beginning with “Front air bags do not provide the”.
cards.back: Front air bags do not provide the side-impact protection described in the handbook’s side-collision discussion.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about collision mitigation, beginning with “If a frontal impact is unavoidable, the handbook recommends”.
cards.back: If a frontal impact is unavoidable, the handbook recommends trying for a glancing collision through steering rather than a direct head-on blow.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about collision mitigation, beginning with “The frontal-impact discussion anticipates air-bag inflation and deflation and”.
cards.back: The frontal-impact discussion anticipates air-bag inflation and deflation and emphasizes belt use and readiness to prevent a second crash.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about injury response, beginning with “Do not move an injured person unless the vehicle”.
cards.back: Do not move an injured person unless the vehicle is burning or immediate danger of another vehicle striking makes movement necessary.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about injury response, beginning with “The handbook prioritizes people who are not”.
cards.back: The handbook prioritizes people who are not already walking and talking, checking breathing before bleeding.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about injury response, beginning with “For bleeding, the handbook advises direct pressure”.
cards.back: For bleeding, the handbook advises direct pressure on the wound using a hand or cloth.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about injury response, beginning with “Give an injured person”.
cards.back: Give an injured person nothing to drink, including water.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about injury response, beginning with “Use a coat or blanket to keep an”.
cards.back: Use a coat or blanket to keep an injured person warm as the handbook’s shock-prevention advice.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about crash reporting, beginning with “Collect the names and addresses of”.
cards.back: Collect the names and addresses of everyone involved and witnesses, including injured people.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about crash reporting, beginning with “Exchange names, addresses, license numbers, vehicle plate and descriptive”.
cards.back: Exchange names, addresses, license numbers, vehicle plate and descriptive information, and available insurer and policy details with the other drivers.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about crash reporting, beginning with “Record vehicle damage and provide crash information”.
cards.back: Record vehicle damage and provide crash information to police or emergency officials when requested.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about crash reporting, beginning with “After striking a parked vehicle, try to find the”.
cards.back: After striking a parked vehicle, try to find the owner; if unsuccessful, leave visible contact information with the crash date and time.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about crash reporting, beginning with “For an injury or death, contact police and give”.
cards.back: For an injury or death, contact police and give crash information at the time of the crash, then notify your insurer as soon as possible.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about crash reporting, beginning with “If injuries prevent the driver completing a”.
cards.back: If injuries prevent the driver completing a crash report, another person may file it.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about crash reporting, beginning with “After damaging unattended property without locating its owner, contact”.
cards.back: After damaging unattended property without locating its owner, contact the nearest law-enforcement agency and leave a note where the owner can find it.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about crash reporting, beginning with “That unattended-property note must list contact details, driver-license”.
cards.back: That unattended-property note must list contact details, driver-license and plate numbers, crash date and time, and damage.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about crash reporting, beginning with “The unattended-property section advises waiting for law enforcement”.
cards.back: The unattended-property section advises waiting for law enforcement and warns that leaving a crash scene is unlawful.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about printed violation ranking, beginning with “The printed injury-and-fatal-crash table ranks careless driving”.
cards.back: The printed injury-and-fatal-crash table ranks careless driving first, close following second and impaired driving third.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about printed violation ranking, beginning with “The same printed table places failure to stop”.
cards.back: The same printed table places failure to stop fourth, improper turns fifth and disobeying traffic controls sixth.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about printed violation ranking, beginning with “The table’s remaining positions are overdriving conditions seventh, reckless”.
cards.back: The table’s remaining positions are overdriving conditions seventh, reckless driving eighth, emerging from an alley ninth and failing to report a crash tenth.
